summary: Fast vector database and search engine written in Rust, for semantic search, recommendations and RAG with rich filtering.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database. It stores points (vectors with a payload) and provides a production-ready API to search and manage them, with extended filtering for semantic matching, faceted search and more.
sixtySeconds.problem: Turning embeddings into a real search or recommendation app needs a fast, reliable store with filters. Qdrant provides that, written in Rust for performance under load.
whoFor: Developers building RAG and semantic search
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for strong filtering, distributed deployment with sharding and replication, official clients in many languages, and agent skills for coding assistants.
requirements: A client library such as qdrant-client for Python

overview: Run the server with Docker on port 6333, then connect with a client, for example QdrantClient(url="http://localhost:6333") in Python. Official clients include Python, Go, Rust and others.
This quick-start container has no authentication and listens on all interfaces, so read the installation and security guides before production.
Qdrant scales with sharding and replication, can resize collections with zero downtime, and offers ready-made agent skills. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
